en: Jupiter is 318 times more massive than Earth, making it the most massive planet in our solar system.
Earth orbits the Sun at an average distance of about 150 million kilometers.
The Moon's gravitational pull is only about one-sixth as strong as the gravity on Earth.
Approximately 1.3 million Earths could fit inside the Sun's massive spherical volume.
Diamond is the hardest natural mineral, scoring a perfect ten on the Mohs hardness scale.
Clay particles are smaller than 0.002 millimeters, making them the absolute smallest soil particles.
The highest officially recorded air temperature on Earth was 56.7 degrees Celsius in Death Valley.
The world's oceans hold about 97 percent of all the liquid water on Earth's surface.
A magnitude 8 earthquake releases roughly 32 times more energy than a magnitude 7 earthquake.
The 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo ejected approximately 10 cubic kilometers of volcanic material.
A Category 5 tropical cyclone has maximum sustained winds of at least 252 kilometers per hour.
Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt, measuring approximately 940 kilometers in diameter.
